symptom: Commits appeared on feat/command-centre-migration that the agent did not make, authored as the founder, already pushed to GitHub. Discovered when `git push` reported 'Everything up-to-date' on an unpushed branch.

cause: An `autogit busy` hook was wired into Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit and PostToolUse events, armed by .autogit.json {mode:auto}. It committed the whole working tree and pushed, authored as the founder, with no review. It ran OUTSIDE the fence: hooks fire around tool calls, not through PreToolUse, so the classifier never saw it. Because Codex runs with sandbox_mode=workspace-write, the reviewer inherited effective commit rights — breaking 'flags, does not fix' structurally.
evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json UserPromptSubmit + PostToolUse ran `autogit busy`; /d/Pi-Dev-Ops/.autogit.json {"mode":"auto"}; commits 4e587bf0 and e9b083f5 authored 'Phill McGurk' containing .omx telemetry and review transcripts
rejected: oh-my-codex notify-hook.js was the committer — ruled out: zero git/exec calls in the script; it is telemetry only. It fed the files autogit then swept up.
A repo git hook did it — ruled out: .git/hooks contains only .sample files
A scheduled task or daemon — ruled out: no matching scheduled task, no autogit process running
blast_reasoning: An unreviewed write+push path to GitHub authoring as the founder. Blast radius is high not because of what it did (telemetry and transcripts) but because of what it COULD do: any file the agent or reviewer touched would be committed and pushed as the founder, bypassing the fence entirely.
approaches: remove all four arming points: 2 settings.json hooks, .autogit.json mode, codex notify hook
reviewer_findings: Not routed to cross-model review: this is infrastructure removal directed by the founder, not a code change under the migration spec.
immunisation: .gitignore now covers .omx/ and .harness/*.txt|*.diff so a future auto-committer cannot re-pollute the branch. SEPARATE FINDING: .harness/incidents.jsonl was itself gitignored by a pre-existing .harness/*.jsonl rule — the entire audit trail was untracked and would have been lost with this machine. Force-tracked.

symptom: Sweep of the deployed dashboard for service-role (RLS-bypassing) Supabase client use, prompted by import drift found during the migration.
loop: grep for createServerClient/createAdminClient call sites; inspect auth model and query scoping; verify proxy matcher covers /api
left_alone: Everything. Reported separately from the migration diff as instructed.
cause: NOT A SECURITY INCIDENT. The dashboard is single-operator: one shared DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, HMAC session cookie, no per-user identity anywhere. No query filters by user_id or auth.uid() because there are no users to separate. Service-role is architecturally consistent with that design, and proxy.ts (Next 16 network-boundary proxy) gates all routes including /api, returning 401 unauthenticated.
evidence: 4 service-role call sites: app/(main)/history/page.tsx, app/api/analyze/route.ts, app/api/sessions/route.ts, lib/supabase/settings.ts. proxy.ts matcher covers all non-static routes. app/api/auth/login/route.ts confirms single shared password.
rejected: Multi-tenant data leak - ruled out: no per-user identity exists in the schema or the auth model
Unauthenticated destructive endpoint - ruled out: proxy.ts matcher covers /api and 401s without a session
blast_reasoning: No change made. Findings are hygiene, not exposure.
approaches: static sweep + auth-model verification
reviewer_findings: Not routed to review: investigation, not a code change.
immunisation: none applied - three observations recorded for separate disposition, deliberately NOT fixed inside the migration diff
gated_on: Founder disposition on three separate items: (1) createCookieServerClient is dead code - defined, called nowhere - implying an RLS path that does not exist; use it or delete it, because leaving it invites the assumption that RLS is in play. (2) DELETE /api/sessions does an unconditional delete-all via service-role using the .neq('id','') delete-everything idiom - authenticated, but no confirmation and no scoping. (3) MIGRATION-RELEVANT: any ported capability that assumed RLS (source used an anon-key RLS client) will silently lose that assumption on the target's service-role client.

symptom: Destructive capability exposed over HTTP is outside every gate built today. Third and fourth unfenced write path, after CI and the auto-commit hook.

cause: The fence intercepts PreToolUse - tool calls. It never sees HTTP. In a single shared-password system 'authenticated' means anything holding the password, including the estate's own agents, so any destructive capability reachable over HTTP sits outside the fence by construction. Compounded because the dashboard's own deployment host was absent from fence.hosts, so even an agent curling it matched no predicate.
evidence: 21 route handlers enumerated. /api/actions spawns child_process with env {...process.env}; /api/actions/commit pushes to GitHub via octokit; /api/sessions DELETE used .neq('id','') delete-all; /api/pi-ceo/[...path] is a catch-all proxy to PI_CEO_URL.
rejected: Command injection in /api/actions - ruled out: fixed binary 'claude', prompt passed as a separate argv element, no shell:true. I initially overstated this as arbitrary execution and corrected it.
Unauthenticated access - ruled out: proxy.ts matcher covers all non-static routes and 401s
blast_reasoning: The spawned CLI inherited 9 credentials including SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, VERCEL_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and DASHBOARD_PASSWORD, in a process driven by a caller-supplied prompt.
approaches: scope the child env to an allowlist; require confirmation or an id on the destructive DELETE; delete the dead RLS client; extend fence hosts
reviewer_findings: Not yet routed to review - infrastructure remediation, separate from the migration diff as instructed.
immunisation: Partial. fence.hosts now includes pi-dev-ops.vercel.app so an AGENT curling the dashboard is caught at the tool layer. This does NOT gate the app calling its own endpoints - the fence never sees those. Closing the class properly needs per-capability auth rather than one shared password, which is a design change.
gated_on: Remaining from the approved order: /api/pi-ceo/[...path] path allowlist (item 2). Then capability 2+3. Design question deferred: per-capability tokens vs one shared DASHBOARD_PASSWORD.
